A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same ExtrinSplat paper and complete supplementary Sections 6–10. All 18 pages are readable. Pages 3–18 are textually and visually identical; differences on pages 1–2 concern authorship notes, the version stamp, and text reflow.

before.justification: v2 reports original LERF object-selection and ScanNet segmentation experiments, ablations, runtime measurements, and supplementary qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains the same original experiments and analyses in the main text and supplementary material.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains identical mask preparation, object grouping, neutral-point filtering, VLM-based feature extraction, and extrinsic-index querying procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same LERF and ScanNet tasks, supplementary Grasp-Net and mobile-phone office scenes, and object-editing demonstrations.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–3 and the supplementary comparisons. Both retain methods including OpenGaussian, InstanceGaussian, Dr.Splat, LAGA, and LUDVIG in the corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: Sections 4 and 6.2 retain identical evaluation procedures, including LERF queries and mask IoU, the same ten ScanNet scenes and 19/15/10-class settings, and disabled Gaussian densification for ScanNet.

E4.justification: The filtering and feature-extraction ablations, sparse-mask tests, VLM and prompt-count comparisons, threshold sensitivity, runtime breakdown, failure cases, and semantic analyses are identical.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The descriptive category-distribution analysis in Section 10.2 is also unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative results are unchanged. For example, both report 54.3 mean LERF mIoU in Table 2, 45.5 ScanNet 19-class mIoU in Table 3, and 555.14 seconds total runtime in Table 9.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 and the mathematical definitions of rendering weights, grouping, semantic entropy, similarity matching, and the extrinsic index are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, and conclusion retain identical claims about decoupling geometry and semantics, supporting polysemy, handling neutral points, and improving efficiency and accuracy.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are identical, including dependence on mask accuracy and VLM judgments, sparse-supervision failures, neutral-point identification difficulties, and viewpoint-dependent semantic features.

D1.justification: Section 6 retains the same implementation details, thresholds, three-view selection, five-noun prompt, and evaluation specifications. Table 9 retains the same V100 hardware disclosure; no resource-access information changes.

R1.justification: The same 36 references and related-work discussions are retained. Positioning against embedding-based approaches and prior boundary-processing methods is unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds equal-contribution credit for Jiayu Ding and Xinpeng Liu and changes Ge Li's corresponding-author marker from an asterisk to a dagger. The version stamp changes, but scientific prose and section organization remain identical.

P2.justification: The author notes move beneath the email addresses, replacing the bottom-of-page corresponding-author footnote and causing limited text reflow across pages 1–2. All figures, tables, and subsequent page layouts remain identical.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies equal-contribution attribution and adjusts the opening layout. The scientific content, experimental evidence, reproducibility information, and appendices are unchanged, so these limited administrative edits do not materially change the paper's overall quality.
